heard: Astronauts floating in orbit are still trapped by Earth's gravity. In 1961, Soviet cosmonaut Gherman Titov reported the first case of space sickness. This sickness occurs even though space is actually not a gravity-free vacuum. At the altitude of the space station, Earth's gravity is nearly 90% as strong as on the ground. Normal gravity on Earth's surface pulls at approximately 9.8 meters per second squared. In orbit, gravity is still highly active, but spacecraft are in constant freefall. High horizontal speed lets them continuously fall over the curving horizon of the Earth. And because they never stop falling around Earth, it feels like...
